In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the blood coagulation serine proteases, thrombin and factor XIa.
the structural basis of thrombin's Na+ dependence.
the molecular mechanism of thrombin allosteric activation and the role of Na+ in the slow → fast transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the self-inhibited thrombin is not a good model for the Na+-free inactive slow form, and that the Na+ ion is not essential for the maintenance of the active fast conformation.
the structure of thrombin without Na+ is a slow conformation that is self-inhibited.
thrombin exists as a dynamic equilibrium among several conformations, and that these conformations are linked by allosteric mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of the self-inhibited confromation is the first crystal structure of a self-inhibited thrombin and the first crystal structure to show a single molecule without any significant packing interactions in the active site and Na+ site regions.

Na+ is not only a key activator for thrombin but also a key inhibitor.

the self-inhibited con-formation of thrombin is a bona fide conformation that is in equilibrium with the slow form.
